functions.name: tinyobj::MaterialReader::~MaterialReader
functions.description: Virtual destructor for the MaterialReader interface. Ensures proper cleanup through base-class pointers.
requirements: May be invoked via a base-class pointer to a derived MaterialReader.
No explicit preconditions; object should have been constructed normally.

functions.name: tinyobj::MaterialReader::operator()
functions.signature: virtual bool tinyobj::MaterialReader::operator()(const std::string &matId, std::vector<material_t> *materials, std::map<std::string, int> *matMap, std::string *warn, std::string *err) = 0
functions.description: Pure virtual callback to load/parse materials identified by matId into the provided containers. Implementations should fill materials and matMap and append any warning/error text. Returns true on success.
requirements: materials must be a non-null pointer to a valid vector to receive parsed materials.
matMap must be a non-null pointer to a valid map to be filled with material name-to-index mapping.
warn and err may be null; if non-null, messages should be appended, not overwritten.
Implementations should return true on success and false on failure.
matId is a material library identifier (usually a filename) and may be used as-is by concrete readers.

functions.name: tinyobj::MaterialFileReader::MaterialFileReader
functions.description: Constructs a MaterialReader that reads .mtl files from a base search path. The path may contain multiple search entries separated by ';' on Windows and ':' on POSIX.
requirements: mtl_basedir may be empty to indicate current/relative directory resolution.
If non-empty and contains multiple entries, they must be separated by the platform-specific separator (';' on Windows, ':' otherwise).

functions.name: tinyobj::MaterialFileReader::~MaterialFileReader
functions.description: Destructor for MaterialFileReader. No special action required.
requirements: Object must have been constructed normally.

functions.name: tinyobj::MaterialFileReader::operator()
functions.signature: virtual bool tinyobj::MaterialFileReader::operator()(const std::string &matId, std::vector<material_t> *materials, std::map<std::string, int> *matMap, std::string *warn, std::string *err)
functions.description: Loads and parses a .mtl file named matId from the configured search path. Populates materials and matMap. On failure, appends a warning indicating the file was not found and returns false.
requirements: materials and matMap must be non-null and point to valid containers.
warn and err may be null; if non-null, diagnostic text may be appended (warnings on not found, parser warnings; errors are not used by this implementation except passed through from LoadMtl).
matId should be a filename (no automatic trimming).
Search path resolution: if mtl_basedir is non-empty and contains multiple entries, each entry is tried in order using JoinPath(entry, matId). If empty, matId is treated as a path.
Requires file to be readable; otherwise returns false.

functions.name: tinyobj::MaterialStreamReader::MaterialStreamReader
functions.description: Constructs a MaterialReader that reads materials from an existing input stream reference.
requirements: inStream must remain valid and in a good state for the lifetime of the MaterialStreamReader and any operator() calls.

functions.name: tinyobj::MaterialStreamReader::~MaterialStreamReader
functions.description: Destructor for MaterialStreamReader. No special action required.
requirements: Object must have been constructed normally.

functions.name: tinyobj::MaterialStreamReader::operator()
functions.signature: virtual bool tinyobj::MaterialStreamReader::operator()(const std::string &matId, std::vector<material_t> *materials, std::map<std::string, int> *matMap, std::string *warn, std::string *err)
functions.description: Parses materials from the bound input stream and fills materials and matMap. Ignores matId. Returns false and emits a warning if the stream is in an error state.
requirements: materials and matMap must be non-null and point to valid containers.
The bound std::istream must be in a good state; otherwise returns false and appends a warning message if warn is non-null.
warn and err may be null; if non-null, messages from LoadMtl are appended.

functions.name: tinyobj::ObjReader::ObjReader
functions.description: Default constructor for the high-level OBJ reader. Initializes internal state (valid_ = false).
requirements: No preconditions. Reader must be used by calling ParseFromFile or ParseFromString before accessing parsed data.

functions.name: tinyobj::ObjReader::ParseFromFile
functions.signature: bool tinyobj::ObjReader::ParseFromFile(const std::string &filename, const ObjReaderConfig &config = ObjReaderConfig())
functions.description: Parses a Wavefront .obj file (and its referenced .mtl files) from disk. Populates internal attrib, shapes, and materials, and records warnings/errors. Returns true on success and sets Valid() accordingly.
requirements: filename must refer to a readable .obj file; failure sets error message and returns false.
config.mtl_search_path: if empty, the directory of filename is used to locate .mtl files; otherwise that path is used.
config.triangulate controls polygon triangulation; config.vertex_color controls vertex color parsing/defaults.
After return, Warning() may contain non-fatal messages; Error() contains fatal errors if any.

functions.name: tinyobj::ObjReader::ParseFromString
functions.signature: bool tinyobj::ObjReader::ParseFromString(const std::string &obj_text, const std::string &mtl_text, const ObjReaderConfig &config = ObjReaderConfig())
functions.description: Parses .obj data from an in-memory string and .mtl data from a second string. Ignores any mtllib filenames in the obj_text and uses mtl_text instead. Populates internal data structures. Returns true on success and sets Valid().
requirements: obj_text should contain the entire OBJ file contents as text.
mtl_text should contain the entire MTL file contents to be used; mtllib statements are ignored in obj_text.
config.triangulate and config.vertex_color influence parsing as in ParseFromFile.
Warning() and Error() may contain messages after return.

functions.name: tinyobj::ObjReader::Valid
functions.description: Indicates whether the last parse succeeded. True after a successful ParseFromFile/ParseFromString call; false otherwise.
requirements: Call after a parse attempt; initial value is false.

functions.name: tinyobj::ObjReader::GetAttrib
functions.description: Returns a const reference to parsed vertex attributes (positions, normals, texcoords, colors, weights, etc.).
requirements: Meaningful only after a successful parse (Valid() == true). Do not modify the returned reference.

functions.name: tinyobj::ObjReader::GetShapes
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the parsed shape list (meshes/lines/points grouped by name/material).
requirements: Meaningful only after a successful parse (Valid() == true). The returned reference remains valid while the ObjReader object is alive.

functions.name: tinyobj::ObjReader::GetMaterials
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the parsed materials array.
requirements: Meaningful only after a successful parse (Valid() == true). Do not modify the returned reference.

functions.name: tinyobj::ObjReader::Warning
functions.description: Returns the warning messages accumulated during the last parse (may be empty).
requirements: Call after a parse attempt; string is owned by the ObjReader and valid as long as it lives.

functions.name: tinyobj::ObjReader::Error
functions.description: Returns the error messages accumulated during the last parse (empty on success).
requirements: Call after a parse attempt; string is owned by the ObjReader and valid as long as it lives.

functions.name: tinyobj::LoadObj
functions.signature: bool tinyobj::LoadObj(tinyobj::attrib_t *attrib, std::vector<tinyobj::shape_t> *shapes, std::vector<tinyobj::material_t> *materials, std::string *warn, std::string *err, const char *filename, const char *mtl_basedir = NULL, bool triangulate = true, bool default_vcols_fallback = true)
functions.description: Legacy v1 API. Loads an OBJ from a file path, optionally specifying an MTL base directory. Fills attrib, shapes, and materials. Returns true on success; warning and error messages are appended to warn/err if provided.
requirements: attrib, shapes, and materials must be non-null and point to valid containers; they will be cleared/overwritten as part of loading.
filename must be a non-null C string referring to a readable file.
mtl_basedir may be NULL; if non-null, it is used as the base directory to search for .mtl files (a trailing path separator will be added if missing).
triangulate controls polygon triangulation behavior; default_vcols_fallback controls whether vertex colors default to white when not present.
warn and err may be null; if non-null, text is appended.

functions.name: tinyobj::LoadObj
functions.signature: bool tinyobj::LoadObj(tinyobj::attrib_t *attrib, std::vector<tinyobj::shape_t> *shapes, std::vector<tinyobj::material_t> *materials, std::string *warn, std::string *err, std::istream *inStream, tinyobj::MaterialReader *readMatFn = NULL, bool triangulate = true, bool default_vcols_fallback = true)
functions.description: Legacy v1 API. Loads an OBJ from an input stream, using an optional MaterialReader to resolve mtllib entries. Fills attrib, shapes, and materials; returns true on success.
requirements: attrib, shapes, and materials must be non-null valid containers; they will be overwritten with parsed data.
inStream must be non-null and readable; the function reads until EOF.
readMatFn may be null; if non-null, it is used to load materials when encountering mtllib directives.
triangulate and default_vcols_fallback control parsing as in the filename overload.
warn and err may be null; if non-null, messages are appended.

functions.name: tinyobj::LoadObjWithCallback
functions.signature: bool tinyobj::LoadObjWithCallback(std::istream &inStream, const tinyobj::callback_t &callback, void *user_data = NULL, tinyobj::MaterialReader *readMatFn = NULL, std::string *warn = NULL, std::string *err = NULL)
functions.description: Legacy v1 callback-based loader. Parses OBJ text from a stream and invokes user callbacks (vertex, normal, texcoord, indices, materials, groups, objects) as elements are encountered. If readMatFn is provided, it is used to load/parse mtllib-referenced materials and mtllib_cb is called with the parsed materials.
requirements: inStream must be readable and supply the OBJ content; the function reads until EOF.
callback may have any subset of function pointers set; null callbacks are simply not invoked.
If readMatFn is non-null and mtllib statements are encountered, readMatFn will be invoked; callback.mtllib_cb will then be called if set.
warn and err may be null; if non-null, diagnostic messages are appended.
user_data is passed through to every callback. The implementation does not dereference user_data.

functions.name: tinyobj::LoadMtl
functions.signature: void tinyobj::LoadMtl(std::map<std::string, int> *material_map, std::vector<tinyobj::material_t> *materials, std::istream *inStream, std::string *warning, std::string *err)
functions.description: Parses a Wavefront .mtl stream and appends materials to materials while updating material_map with name-to-index entries. Emits warnings for issues (e.g., both d and Tr present).
requirements: material_map and materials must be non-null and point to valid containers; a default material is always created and pushed at the end.
inStream must be non-null and readable; the function consumes the stream until EOF.
warning and err may be null; if non-null, strings are assigned warning text (and may be appended internally).
Input lines should be UTF-8; a leading BOM is stripped if present on the first line.

functions.name: tinyobj::ParseTextureNameAndOption
functions.description: Parses a texture filename and its inline options from an MTL texture map line, filling texname and texopt. Supports standard options (e.g., -o, -s, -t, -clamp, -mm, -imfchan, -type, -texres, -bm) and the tinyobjloader '-colorspace' extension. Returns true if a texture name was found.
requirements: texname and texopt must be non-null pointers to writable objects.
linebuf must be a non-null, null-terminated C string containing the entire line to parse (options followed by filename; filename may contain spaces and is assumed to extend to end of line).
texopt is expected to be pre-initialized to defaults appropriate for the texture kind (e.g., via InitTexOpt in this codebase), although the function also sets many fields explicitly.
Returns true when a texture name is found; false otherwise.

data_types.description: A string representing a file system path or base directory. May be absolute or relative, and may include multiple search entries separated by ';' on Windows or ':' on POSIX. Used to locate files such as .mtl or .obj.
Text content of a Wavefront .obj file. Lines contain statements like v/vt/vn, f, o/g/usemtl/mtllib, etc. Parsed as ASCII/UTF-8 text until EOF.
Text content of a Wavefront .mtl material library. Contains directives like newmtl, Ka/Kd/Ks/Ke, Ns, d/Tr, map_* with options, etc. Parsed as ASCII/UTF-8 text until EOF.

A single MTL map_* option line segment consisting of texture options followed by a texture filename. May include options such as -o, -s, -t, -clamp, -mm, -imfchan, -type, -texres, -bm, and '-colorspace', followed by a filename that may include spaces; treated as a null-terminated C string.

import os
import random
import sys
from typing import List

# This generator targets inputs used as filesystem paths and filenames for tinyobjloader fuzz stubs.
# It produces valid, interesting path strings and minimal valid OBJ/MTL file contents when the
# fuzzer requests a filename-backed buffer. The harness will place the returned bytes into a file
# and pass its filename to the target. We therefore emit content that can be either:
# - OBJ text (so LoadObj on a filename can succeed and exercise parsing), or
# - MTL text (so MaterialFileReader::operator() can parse materials), or
# - A search path string (used by MaterialFileReader constructor), or
# - An empty or edge-case path string.
#
# Strategy:
# - Randomly choose among several profiles to cover different code paths:
#   1) Minimal, valid OBJ that references an inline MTL via mtllib, plus embedded MTL content
#      placed in the same buffer separated by a marker line that a typical harness may split.
#      Since the stubs use FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME for file-backed inputs, we focus on producing
#      standalone valid OBJ or MTL payloads; the harness typically uses the exact bytes as the
#      file content (filename is generated by the framework). The base-dir strings are provided
#      via FUZZ_PARAM_STR; they do not come from this buffer directly, but supplying different
#      content types helps overall corpus growth when reused across stubs.
#   2) Standalone valid MTL content to exercise MaterialFileReader and LoadMtl.
#   3) Edge-case but valid path-like content (multiple search entries) that can also serve as
#      small, parseable MTL, keeping it valid text if read as a file.
#   4) Larger OBJ with multiple shapes, groups, faces, normals, texcoords, materials.
# - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.
# - Use only standard library, no I/O.

def _rand_choice(rng: random.Random, items: List[str]) -> str:
    return items[rng.randrange(len(items))]

def _gen_valid_mtl(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Produce a valid MTL with several entries and options supported by tinyobj
    names = ["mat", "default", "metal", "plastic", "wood", "glass"]
    texs = ["tex.png", "albedo.jpg", "normal.tga", "roughness.png", "ao.bmp"]
    lines = []
    # Add comments and possible BOM handling via leading comment; BOM stripped by loader if present.
    lines.append("# Example MTL generated\n")
    # First material
    mname1 = _rand_choice(rng, names) + str(rng.randrange(100))
    lines.append(f"newmtl {mname1}\n")
    lines.append(f"Ns {rng.uniform(1.0, 1000.0):.1f}\n")
    lines.append(f"Ni {rng.uniform(1.0, 2.5):.3f}\n")
    lines.append(f"d {rng.uniform(0.0, 1.0):.3f}\n")
    # Also include Tr sometimes (loader warns when both d and Tr present)
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        lines.append(f"Tr {rng.uniform(0.0, 1.0):.3f}\n")
    lines.append(f"illum {rng.randrange(0, 10)}\n")
    lines.append(f"Ka {rng.random():.3f} {rng.random():.3f} {rng.random():.3f}\n")
    lines.append(f"Kd {rng.random():.3f} {rng.random():.3f} {rng.random():.3f}\n")
    lines.append(f"Ks {rng.random():.3f} {rng.random():.3f} {rng.random():.3f}\n")
    # Texture with options
    texname = _rand_choice(rng, texs)
    # Include options supported: -o, -s, -clamp, -mm, -imfchan, -type, -texres, -bm, and extension -colorspace
    ox, oy, oz = (rng.uniform(-1, 1) for _ in range(3))
    sx, sy, sz = (rng.uniform(0.1, 3.0) for _ in range(3))
    mm_base, mm_gain = rng.uniform(0.0, 1.0), rng.uniform(0.5, 2.0)
    clamp = _rand_choice(rng, ["on", "off"])
    imfchan = _rand_choice(rng, list("rgbmaRGBMA"))
    ttype = _rand_choice(rng, ["sphere", "cube", "rectangle"])  # accepted as pass-through
    texres = rng.choice([64, 128, 256, 512, 1024])
    bm = rng.uniform(0.1, 2.0)
    colorspace = _rand_choice(rng, ["sRGB", "linear", "auto"])
    lines.append(
        f"map_Kd -o {ox:.3f} {oy:.3f} {oz:.3f} -s {sx:.3f} {sy:.3f} {sz:.3f} "
        f"-clamp {clamp} -mm {mm_base:.3f} {mm_gain:.3f} -imfchan {imfchan} "
        f"-type {ttype} -texres {texres} -bm {bm:.3f} -colorspace {colorspace} {texname}\n"
    )
    # Second material
    mname2 = _rand_choice(rng, names) + str(rng.randrange(100))
    lines.append(f"newmtl {mname2}\n")
    lines.append(f"Kd 1.000 1.000 1.000\n")
    lines.append(f"map_Ks { _rand_choice(rng, texs) }\n")
    # Default material is appended by loader; we just provide realistic content.
    return "".join(lines)

def _gen_valid_obj(rng: random.Random, with_mtllib: bool = True) -> str:
    # Generate a small but valid OBJ with vertices, normals, texcoords, faces, groups, usemtl
    lines = []
    lines.append("# Example OBJ generated\n")
    if with_mtllib:
        lines.append("mtllib inline.mtl\n")
    # Vertices
    for i in range(1, 9):
        x, y, z = rng.uniform(-1, 1), rng.uniform(-1, 1), rng.uniform(-1, 1)
        lines.append(f"v {x:.5f} {y:.5f} {z:.5f}\n")
    # Vertex colors optionally (supported by tinyobj when enabled)
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        for i in range(1, 5):
            r, g, b = rng.random(), rng.random(), rng.random()
            lines.append(f"v {rng.uniform(-1,1):.5f} {rng.uniform(-1,1):.5f} {rng.uniform(-1,1):.5f} {r:.3f} {g:.3f} {b:.3f}\n")
    # Normals and texcoords
    for i in range(1, 6):
        nx, ny, nz = rng.uniform(-1, 1), rng.uniform(-1, 1), rng.uniform(-1, 1)
        lines.append(f"vn {nx:.5f} {ny:.5f} {nz:.5f}\n")
    for i in range(1, 6):
        u, v = rng.random(), rng.random()
        lines.append(f"vt {u:.5f} {v:.5f}\n")
    lines.append("o Object001\n")
    lines.append("g GroupA\n")
    lines.append("usemtl mat0\n")
    # Faces referencing indices; use various index forms
    # Ensure at least 8 vertices and 5 tex/normals available
    faces = [
        "f 1/1/1 2/2/2 3/3/3\n",
        "f 4//4 5//5 6//1\n",
        "f 7/4 8/5 1/1\n",
        "f 2 3 4\n",
    ]
    lines.extend(faces)
    # Add a quad to trigger triangulation optionally
    lines.append("usemtl mat1\n")
    lines.append("f 5/2/3 6/3/4 7/4/5 8/5/1\n")
    # Lines and points primitives
    lines.append("l 1 2 3 4\n")
    lines.append("p 6 7 8\n")
    return "".join(lines)

def _gen_search_path_string(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Generate a cross-platform search path list (Windows uses ';', POSIX ':').
    # We include both separators occasionally; implementations typically treat platform-specific,
    # but providing either remains a valid string.
    sep = rng.choice([';', ':'])
    parts = []
    bases = [".", "..", "assets", "models", "data", "mtl", "obj", "textures"]
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 5)):
        base = _rand_choice(rng, bases)
        sub = _rand_choice(rng, ["", "sub", "set", "pack", "a", "b"]) \
              + ("" if rng.random() < 0.5 else str(rng.randrange(10)))
        if sub:
            parts.append(base + "/" + sub)
        else:
            parts.append(base)
    # Mix in absolute-like and Windows-like entries sometimes
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        parts.append("/usr/share/mtl")
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        parts.append("C:\\mtl\\packs")
    return sep.join(parts)

def _compose_inline_obj_and_mtl(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Some harnesses only take a single file; we cannot create multiple files, so we
    # emit a valid OBJ by itself. However, in case the harness routes the same buffer
    # to different FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME consumers, we can also concatenate with a marker
    # the MTL content so either part is still parseable as text when read entirely.
    obj = _gen_valid_obj(rng, with_mtllib=True)
    mtl = _gen_valid_mtl(rng)
    # Keep size bound
    combined = obj
    marker = "\n# ---INLINE-MTL---\n"
    if len(obj) + len(marker) + len(mtl) <= 4000 and rng.random() < 0.7:
        combined = obj + marker + mtl
    return combined

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose a profile
    mode = rng.randrange(5)
    if mode == 0:
        # Minimal OBJ without mtllib (for ParseFromString paths that ignore mtllib)
        content = _gen_valid_obj(rng, with_mtllib=False)
    elif mode == 1:
        # OBJ with mtllib and concatenated MTL
        content = _compose_inline_obj_and_mtl(rng)
    elif mode == 2:
        # Standalone MTL content
        content = _gen_valid_mtl(rng)
    elif mode == 3:
        # Search path string; still valid text file content
        content = _gen_search_path_string(rng) + "\n"
    else:
        # Larger OBJ with more faces and groups
        content = _gen_valid_obj(rng, with_mtllib=True)
        # Duplicate some elements to increase complexity
        extras = []
        for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
            extras.append("g ExtraGroup\n")
            extras.append("usemtl extra\n")
            extras.append("f 1/1/1 4/2/2 7/3/3\n")
        content += "".join(extras)
    # Ensure size limit
    b = content.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')[:4096]
    return b

import random
import string
from typing import List, Tuple

# This generator creates valid Wavefront OBJ text, optionally with an accompanying MTL text
# concatenated with a delimiter so either half can be selected by the fuzzer harness that calls
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR() multiple times. Since the harness requests separate strings for OBJ and MTL,
# we produce a single coherent blob that contains both texts; each FUZZ_PARAM_STR will fetch a
# random slice from the buffer. To maximize usefulness, we place the OBJ first, then two newlines,
# then the MTL so that taking the head or the tail yields valid content for either.
# For FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME, we embed a plausible .obj filename followed by a NUL and then embed
# the actual OBJ data so that reading by filename-based fuzzers that map the provided filename
# into test content can still find an .obj-like name while the bytes remain useful text.

MAX_BYTES = 4096

def _rand_name(rng: random.Random, prefix: str, max_len: int = 12) -> str:
    body = ''.join(rng.choices(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_-", k=rng.randint(1, max_len)))
    return f"{prefix}{body}"

def _rand_color(rng: random.Random) -> Tuple[float, float, float]:
    # Wide gamut in [0,1], sometimes >1 to test HDR params in MTL (still valid floats)
    if rng.random() < 0.15:
        return (rng.uniform(0.0, 2.0), rng.uniform(0.0, 2.0), rng.uniform(0.0, 2.0))
    return (rng.random(), rng.random(), rng.random())

def _fmt_f(f: float) -> str:
    # Compact float formatting for OBJ/MTL
    return ("%g" % f)

def _gen_vertices(rng: random.Random, n_v: int, with_color: bool, with_w: bool) -> List[str]:
    lines = []
    for _ in range(n_v):
        x, y, z = (rng.uniform(-10, 10) for _ in range(3))
        parts = ["v", _fmt_f(x), _fmt_f(y), _fmt_f(z)]
        if with_w and rng.random() < 0.5:
            parts.append(_fmt_f(rng.uniform(0.1, 5.0)))
        if with_color and rng.random() < 0.8:
            r, g, b = _rand_color(rng)
            parts += [_fmt_f(r), _fmt_f(g), _fmt_f(b)]
        lines.append(" ".join(parts))
    return lines

def _gen_texcoords(rng: random.Random, n_vt: int) -> List[str]:
    lines = []
    for _ in range(n_vt):
        u = rng.random()
        v = rng.random()
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            w = rng.random()
            lines.append(f"vt {_fmt_f(u)} {_fmt_f(v)} {_fmt_f(w)}")
        else:
            lines.append(f"vt {_fmt_f(u)} {_fmt_f(v)}")
    return lines

def _gen_normals(rng: random.Random, n_vn: int) -> List[str]:
    lines = []
    for _ in range(n_vn):
        nx, ny, nz = (rng.uniform(-1, 1) for _ in range(3))
        lines.append(f"vn {_fmt_f(nx)} {_fmt_f(ny)} {_fmt_f(nz)}")
    return lines

def _tri(rng: random.Random, vi: List[int], vti: List[int], vni: List[int]) -> str:
    # Compose an f line with mixed presence of vt/vn indices
    def pick(i: int) -> Tuple[int, int, int]:
        return (
            rng.choice(vi) if vi else 0,
            rng.choice(vti) if vti and rng.random() < 0.8 else None,
            rng.choice(vni) if vni and rng.random() < 0.8 else None,
        )
    a = pick(0); b = pick(1); c = pick(2)
    def fmt(t: Tuple[int,int,int]) -> str:
        v, vt, vn = t
        if vt is None and vn is None:
            return f"{v}"
        if vt is None:
            return f"{v}//{vn}"
        if vn is None:
            return f"{v}/{vt}"
        return f"{v}/{vt}/{vn}"
    return f"f {fmt(a)} {fmt(b)} {fmt(c)}"

def _poly(rng: random.Random, vi: List[int], vti: List[int], vni: List[int], sides: int) -> str:
    parts = []
    for _ in range(sides):
        v = rng.choice(vi)
        has_vt = vti and rng.random() < 0.7
        has_vn = vni and rng.random() < 0.7
        vt = rng.choice(vti) if has_vt else None
        vn = rng.choice(vni) if has_vn else None
        if vt is None and vn is None:
            parts.append(f"{v}")
        elif vt is None:
            parts.append(f"{v}//{vn}")
        elif vn is None:
            parts.append(f"{v}/{vt}")
        else:
            parts.append(f"{v}/{vt}/{vn}")
    return "f " + " ".join(parts)

def _gen_faces(rng: random.Random, n_faces: int, n_gons_ratio: float, vi: List[int], vti: List[int], vni: List[int]) -> List[str]:
    lines = []
    for _ in range(n_faces):
        if rng.random() < n_gons_ratio:
            sides = rng.randint(4, 7)
            lines.append(_poly(rng, vi, vti, vni, sides))
        else:
            lines.append(_tri(rng, vi, vti, vni))
    return lines

def _gen_edges_points(rng: random.Random, vi: List[int], vti: List[int]) -> List[str]:
    lines = []
    # Lines (l) may reference v or v/vt
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
            count = rng.randint(2, 5)
            parts = []
            for __ in range(count):
                v = rng.choice(vi)
                if vti and rng.random() < 0.5:
                    parts.append(f"{v}/{rng.choice(vti)}")
                else:
                    parts.append(f"{v}")
            lines.append("l " + " ".join(parts))
    # Points (p)
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        count = rng.randint(1, 6)
        pts = " ".join(str(rng.choice(vi)) for _ in range(count))
        lines.append("p " + pts)
    return lines

def _gen_groups_objs(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    lines = []
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        if rng.random() < 0.6:
            lines.append(f"o {_rand_name(rng, 'obj_')}")
        if rng.random() < 0.9:
            # Multiple group names allowed on one line
            names = [_rand_name(rng, 'grp_') for __ in range(rng.randint(1, 3))]
            lines.append("g " + " ".join(names))
    return lines

def _gen_mtllib_usemtl(rng: random.Random, mtllib_name: str, material_names: List[str]) -> List[str]:
    lines = []
    lines.append(f"mtllib {mtllib_name}")
    # use materials before shapes to test switching
    for m in material_names:
        if rng.random() < 0.8:
            lines.append(f"usemtl {m}")
    return lines

def _gen_smoothing(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    lines = []
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            lines.append("s off")
        else:
            lines.append(f"s {rng.randint(1, 8)}")
    return lines

def _gen_mtl(rng: random.Random, material_names: List[str]) -> str:
    lines = []
    # Optional comments and newlines
    lines.append("# Generated MTL")
    for name in material_names:
        lines.append(f"newmtl {name}")
        # Basic properties
        Ka = _rand_color(rng)
        Kd = _rand_color(rng)
        Ks = _rand_color(rng)
        Tf = _rand_color(rng) if rng.random() < 0.3 else (1.0, 1.0, 1.0)
        Ns = rng.uniform(1.0, 1000.0)
        Ni = rng.uniform(0.1, 4.0)
        d = rng.uniform(0.0, 1.0)
        Tr = 1.0 - d if rng.random() < 0.5 else None
        illum = rng.randint(0, 10)
        lines.append(f"Ka {_fmt_f(Ka[0])} {_fmt_f(Ka[1])} {_fmt_f(Ka[2])}")
        lines.append(f"Kd {_fmt_f(Kd[0])} {_fmt_f(Kd[1])} {_fmt_f(Kd[2])}")
        lines.append(f"Ks {_fmt_f(Ks[0])} {_fmt_f(Ks[1])} {_fmt_f(Ks[2])}")
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            lines.append(f"Tf {_fmt_f(Tf[0])} {_fmt_f(Tf[1])} {_fmt_f(Tf[2])}")
        lines.append(f"Ns {_fmt_f(Ns)}")
        lines.append(f"Ni {_fmt_f(Ni)}")
        lines.append(f"d {_fmt_f(d)}")
        if Tr is not None:
            lines.append(f"Tr {_fmt_f(Tr)}")
        lines.append(f"illum {illum}")
        # Texture maps with options
        texbase = _rand_name(rng, 'tex_', 8)
        # -o offset, -s scale, -clamp, -bm, -imfchan, -type, -texres, -colorspace
        if rng.random() < 0.9:
            lines.append(
                f"map_Kd -o {_fmt_f(rng.uniform(-1,1))} {_fmt_f(rng.uniform(-1,1))} 0 "
                f"-s {_fmt_f(rng.uniform(0.1,2))} {_fmt_f(rng.uniform(0.1,2))} 1 -clamp {rng.choice(['on','off'])} "
                f"-mm {_fmt_f(rng.uniform(0,1))} {_fmt_f(rng.uniform(1,2))} -imfchan {rng.choice(['l','r','g','b','m','z'])} "
                f"-type {rng.choice(['sphere','cube_top','cube_bottom','cube_front','cube_back','cube_left','cube_right'])} "
                f"-texres {rng.choice([64,128,256,512])} -bm {_fmt_f(rng.uniform(0.1,2))} -colorspace {rng.choice(['sRGB','linear'])} "
                f"{texbase}_kd.png")
        if rng.random() < 0.6:
            lines.append(f"map_Ks {texbase}_ks.jpg")
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            lines.append(f"map_Ns -bm {_fmt_f(rng.uniform(0.2,1.5))} {texbase}_ns.png")
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            lines.append(f"bump -bm {_fmt_f(rng.uniform(0.2,1.5))} {texbase}_bump.tga")
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            lines.append(f"map_d {texbase}_alpha.png")
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            lines.append(f"disp {texbase}_disp.exr")
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            lines.append(f"refl -type cube_top {texbase}_refl.hdr")
        lines.append("")
    return "\n".join(lines).rstrip() + "\n"

def _gen_obj_and_mtl(rng: random.Random) -> Tuple[str, str]:
    # Scene sizes
    n_v = rng.randint(8, 40)
    n_vt = rng.randint(0, 24)
    n_vn = rng.randint(0, 24)
    with_color = rng.random() < 0.6
    with_w = rng.random() < 0.3

    obj_lines: List[str] = []
    obj_lines.append("# Generated OBJ")

    # mtllib and usemtl
    mtl_name = _rand_name(rng, "materials_", 10) + ".mtl"
    material_names = [_rand_name(rng, "mat_", 8) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 4))]
    obj_lines += _gen_mtllib_usemtl(rng, mtl_name, material_names)

    # vertices, texcoords, normals
    obj_lines += _gen_vertices(rng, n_v, with_color, with_w)
    if n_vt:
        obj_lines += _gen_texcoords(rng, n_vt)
    if n_vn:
        obj_lines += _gen_normals(rng, n_vn)

    # parameter space vertices (vp) occasionally
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
            obj_lines.append(f"vp {_fmt_f(rng.random())} {_fmt_f(rng.random())}")

    # Groups/objects and smoothing
    obj_lines += _gen_groups_objs(rng)
    obj_lines += _gen_smoothing(rng)

    # Face indices are 1-based
    vi = list(range(1, n_v + 1))
    vti = list(range(1, n_vt + 1)) if n_vt > 0 else []
    vni = list(range(1, n_vn + 1)) if n_vn > 0 else []

    # Generate faces, lines, points
    n_faces = rng.randint(4, 20)
    obj_lines += _gen_faces(rng, n_faces, n_gons_ratio=0.4, vi=vi, vti=vti, vni=vni)
    obj_lines += _gen_edges_points(rng, vi, vti)

    # Switch materials mid-file
    if len(material_names) > 1 and rng.random() < 0.8:
        obj_lines.append(f"usemtl {rng.choice(material_names)}")
        obj_lines += _gen_faces(rng, rng.randint(2, 6), 0.2, vi, vti, vni)

    # Subelements: object rename and group split
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        obj_lines.append(f"o {_rand_name(rng, 'obj_')}")
        obj_lines += _gen_faces(rng, rng.randint(2, 5), 0.5, vi, vti, vni)

    obj_text = "\n".join(obj_lines).rstrip() + "\n"
    mtl_text = _gen_mtl(rng, material_names)
    return obj_text, mtl_text


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Generate coherent OBJ and MTL contents
    obj_text, mtl_text = _gen_obj_and_mtl(rng)

    # Sometimes make an alternate variant stressing different features (quads only, no normals)
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        rng2 = random.Random(seed ^ 0xA5A5)
        obj2, mtl2 = _gen_obj_and_mtl(rng2)
        # Mix in to increase diversity while remaining valid
        obj_text = obj_text + "\n# Variant\n" + obj2
        mtl_text = mtl_text + "\n# Variant\n" + mtl2

    # Compose final buffer: OBJ, separator, MTL. Keep within MAX_BYTES
    sep = "\n\n"  # clear split point
    blob = obj_text + sep + mtl_text

    # Ensure size cap
    data = blob.encode('utf-8')[:MAX_BYTES]

    # If extremely small (edge case), pad with comment lines to ensure parsers see something meaningful
    if len(data) < 64:
        pad_lines = ["# pad", "v 0 0 0", "f 1 1 1"]
        extra = ("\n".join(pad_lines) + "\n").encode('utf-8')
        data = (data + extra)[:MAX_BYTES]

    return data

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for MTL texture option line (options followed by a filename)
# Focus: cover combinations of supported options and edge cases while remaining valid.

IMFCHANS = ['r', 'g', 'b', 'm', 'l', 'z']  # common/implied channels (m=matte, l=luminance)
TYPES = ['sphere', 'cube_top', 'cube_bottom', 'cube_front', 'cube_back', 'cube_left', 'cube_right', 'bump', 'decal', 'displacement', 'specular']
COLORSPACES = ['linear', 'sRGB', 'AdobeRGB', 'ACEScg']
CLAMP = ['on', 'off']

# Some plausible texture filenames, with and without spaces, various extensions
BASE_FILENAMES = [
    'albedo.png', 'normal.jpg', 'roughness.tif', 'metal.exr', 'height.bmp', 'mask.tga', 'diffuse.jpeg',
    'tex with spaces.png', '日本語_テクスチャ.png', 'C:\\textures\\brick_normal.png', './textures/brick_diffuse.png',
    '../assets/wood/wood base color.jpg', 'tile_#1.png', 'weird name (v2).dds'
]

# Utility to maybe add quotes around filename containing spaces; MTL generally allows spaces to end-of-line,
# but adding quotes can explore parser behavior if supported (filename extends to end-of-line regardless).

def build_filename(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    name = rng.choice(BASE_FILENAMES)
    # Optionally append query-like or subpath parts to extend filename
    suffix_opts = ['', '', '', '?v=1', '#chan=r', '.mip1', '.mip0']
    name = name + rng.choice(suffix_opts)
    # Occasionally surround with spaces inside name to test "spaces to end-of-line" behavior
    if ' ' not in name and rng.random() < 0.3:
        insert_pos = rng.randrange(1, len(name))
        name = name[:insert_pos] + ' ' + name[insert_pos:]
    # Optionally quote (some parsers ignore quotes; tinyobj treats filename to EOL, so quotes become part of name)
    if rng.random() < 0.15:
        name = '"' + name + '"'
    return name


def ffloat(rng: random.Random, lo: float, hi: float) -> str:
    # produce compact float strings
    val = rng.uniform(lo, hi)
    # occasionally integer-looking
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        return str(int(round(val)))
    # occasionally scientific
    if rng.random() < 0.1:
        return f"{val:.6e}"
    # normal decimal
    return ("%.6f" % val).rstrip('0').rstrip('.')


def vec3(rng: random.Random, lo: float, hi: float) -> List[str]:
    return [ffloat(rng, lo, hi) for _ in range(3)]


def maybe(opt: str, include_prob: float, rng: random.Random) -> bool:
    return rng.random() < include_prob


def build_options(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    parts: List[str] = []

    # Translation (-o), Scale (-s), Turbulence/Texture origin (-t)
    if maybe('-o', 0.8, rng):
        parts += ['-o'] + vec3(rng, -10.0, 10.0)
    if maybe('-s', 0.85, rng):
        parts += ['-s'] + vec3(rng, 0.001, 10.0)
    if maybe('-t', 0.5, rng):
        parts += ['-t'] + vec3(rng, -1.0, 1.0)

    # Clamp
    if maybe('-clamp', 0.6, rng):
        parts += ['-clamp', rng.choice(CLAMP)]

    # mm (base gain and multiplier)
    if maybe('-mm', 0.7, rng):
        parts += ['-mm', ffloat(rng, 0.0, 2.0), ffloat(rng, 0.0, 4.0)]

    # imfchan
    if maybe('-imfchan', 0.5, rng):
        parts += ['-imfchan', rng.choice(IMFCHANS)]

    # type
    if maybe('-type', 0.4, rng):
        parts += ['-type', rng.choice(TYPES)]

    # texres
    if maybe('-texres', 0.5, rng):
        # common power-of-two or arbitrary
        choices = [64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, rng.randint(16, 4096)]
        parts += ['-texres', str(rng.choice(choices))]

    # bump multiplier (-bm)
    if maybe('-bm', 0.6, rng):
        parts += ['-bm', ffloat(rng, 0.0, 5.0)]

    # tinyobjloader extension: -colorspace
    if maybe('-colorspace', 0.8, rng):
        parts += ['-colorspace', rng.choice(COLORSPACES)]

    # Randomly shuffle some independent groups to vary ordering (keeping each option token with its args)
    # We'll keep the sequence as constructed; OBJ allows arbitrary order of options before filename.
    return parts


def assemble_line(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    parts = build_options(rng)

    # Insert occasional extra spaces or tabs between options
    def join_with_irregular_spacing(items: List[str]) -> str:
        out = []
        for i, tok in enumerate(items):
            out.append(tok)
            if i != len(items) - 1:
                # pick separator: 1+ spaces or a tab
                if rng.random() < 0.15:
                    out.append('\t')
                else:
                    out.append(' ' * rng.randint(1, 3))
        return ''.join(out)

    opt_str = join_with_irregular_spacing(parts) if parts else ''

    # Ensure at least one space before filename when options present
    if opt_str:
        # Occasionally prefix with leading spaces
        if rng.random() < 0.2:
            opt_str = ' ' * rng.randint(1, 3) + opt_str
        # Occasionally suffix with spaces before filename
        opt_str = opt_str + (' ' * rng.randint(1, 3))

    filename = build_filename(rng)

    # Optionally prepend a map type keyword to simulate a full MTL line; parser expects only options+filename,
    # but it tolerates arbitrary leading tokens as part of the line buffer before filename parsing begins.
    # We keep it minimal to remain valid for texture option parsing context created by the fuzzer stub.
    prefix = ''
    if rng.random() < 0.1:
        prefix = rng.choice(['', '  '])  # small indentation

    line = prefix + opt_str + filename

    # Trim to max size to respect 4096 bytes limit
    return line[:4096]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Create several styles and pick one to diversify outcomes deterministically per seed
    styles = []
    for _ in range(4):
        styles.append(assemble_line(rng))

    line = rng.choice(styles)

    # Ensure null-terminated behavior in C string users; Python bytes don't need NUL, but keeping as pure line
    # The fuzzer stub concatenates this line after predefined options; ensure our contribution is a plausible filename
    # or trailing extra options + filename to exercise parsing.

    return line.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
